## CEO BRIEFING

**For:** Dana Whitfield, ahead of the 15:00 board call
**Incident:** INC-2026-1109-01 | **Status at 14:20 UTC, 9 Nov 2026:** OPEN — mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established
**Prepared by:** Incident Commander

### What happened

- **11:42 UTC** — First alert: elevated error rate on the Batch API (bulk job submission endpoint), returning `502` responses. This is the incident start time.
- **11:44** — Confirmed the errors were confined to one of the two independent worker fleets serving Batch API traffic. The other fleet was serving normally throughout.
- **11:47** — Upstream object-storage provider ruled out (their status page green; our Files API, which uses the same provider, stayed healthy).
- **12:58** — **Mitigation applied.** All Batch API traffic cut over to the healthy fleet; the degraded fleet was drained and held out of rotation. Error rate fell to 0.4% within two minutes (baseline for this endpoint is 0.2%).
- **13:00–14:30** — Verification window. Policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before an incident may be declared resolved. Error rate has held at 0.3–0.4% (0.3% at 14:12).

### Who is hit

All figures from `customer-impact.csv`, covering the incident window 11:42–12:58 UTC.

| Measure | Figure |
|---|---|
| Batch API requests in window | **58,900** |
| Failed Batch API requests | **17,602** |
| **Headline impact (failed ÷ total Batch API requests)** | **29.9%** |
| Batch API share of all Northstar traffic in window (842,000 requests) | **~7.0%** |
| Accounts affected | **7 of 9** accounts that use the Batch API (7 of 36 total accounts) |
| Accounts unaffected | 2 Batch API accounts saw zero failures; the other 27 accounts made no Batch API calls in the window |

- Other API surfaces (Inference, Embeddings, Files) are not part of this incident.
- Per-account figures: stark-industries 5,180/14,200; **contoso 3,410/9,400 (36.3%)**; wayne-enterprises 2,790/7,850; globex 2,240/6,100; wonka-industries 2,020/5,900; umbrella-health 1,560/4,300; initech 402/1,150.

### Root cause — not established

Two candidate explanations remain live and **neither has been tested**:

1. **(Leading)** A release shipped at 11:31 lowered the batch worker's database connection-pool ceiling from 80 to 24 per worker; workers on the degraded fleet were observed queueing on database connections. Against this: the same release went to both fleets and only one degraded.
2. **(Secondary)** A concentrated load spike on the affected fleet from ~11:38, running at roughly 3x the morning average. Against this: that fleet absorbed a higher peak on 3 November without elevated errors.

The two may interact, but that is untested as well. Upstream storage was rejected at 11:47. We deliberately did not roll back the release at 12:31 because doing so would have destroyed the evidence needed to test the hypothesis and would have left us unable to distinguish cause from coincidence — the mitigation (moving traffic) fixed customers without that trade-off.

### What is still open at 14:20

- Verification window closes **14:30**. Nothing can be called resolved before then, at the earliest.
- Root cause untested; the rollback test has not been run.
- The degraded fleet is still out of rotation and not returned to service.
- Re-drive of failed jobs during the window: **~60% complete as of 13:52**, no failures observed on re-drive.

### Customer / commercial exposure

- **Contoso** is the only affected account on a contract carrying service-level credits (Schedule B). Two tickets today: **TKT-8903** (11:58, reporting the failures) and **TKT-8907** (12:26, asking where they stand on credits and whether the 99.9% commitment will be breached).
- Under **Schedule B.5**, Monthly Availability for November is determined by Northstar **after the end of the calendar month** and published within 10 business days of month end; Contoso has 30 days from that publication to claim. **No determination has been or can be made today**, and I have not offered one. My reply to Contoso restates that process only.
- For awareness (not for the board unless you want it): Contoso has an older open ticket (**TKT-8841**, 4 Nov) recording that their integration was retrying failed batch submits with no backoff and tripping rate limits, with a fix still queued behind their Q4 freeze. Schedule B.2(b)/(c) exclusions and B.6 disputes exist in the contract. Whether any volume is ever excluded is a month-end commercial/legal judgement — not something to raise with Contoso today, and not something I have asserted.
- The other six affected accounts are on standard terms with no credit clause.

### What you can say at 15:00 (approved by Tomas and Ruth — this is the complete cleared list)

1. There is an incident affecting the Batch API, and it started at 11:42 UTC.
2. A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering.
3. We are monitoring before confirming recovery.
4. A further update will follow, with a stated time.
5. To a named customer, that customer's own impact figures only.

### What not to say

- **Do not state a root cause.** It is untested. (Our status page wrongly said cause was identified at 12:05 — see below.)
- **Do not call it resolved before 14:30**, and not then unless the window closes clean.
- **Do not publish the 29.9% aggregate figure externally** — it is not on the cleared list. It is internal and available to you.
- **Do not mention the two worker fleets externally** — fleet assignment is an internal deployment detail, not a product tier, and customers are not told about it.
- The "~16:00 fully wrapped up" figure is Marcus's internal planning estimate only and has been explicitly marked not for external use.

### One thing to know about our public communications

The status page has had **no update since 12:05** (75 minutes), and that 12:05 post claimed we had *identified the cause* and would be *fully restored within the hour* — neither of which is true or supportable. Marcus flagged this to Ruth at 12:09 and further cause statements were frozen. **I am publishing a corrected update at 14:20**, using only the cleared list, superseding the 12:05 post. If the board has seen the status page, that is the discrepancy to be aware of.

### Separately — confidential, unrelated to this incident

While reading worker configuration during triage, Marcus found the batch worker's database role holds read **and write** access to the billing schema, which it has no legitimate reason to touch. It played **no part** in this incident. Ticket **SEC-411** is raised, Marcus owns it, target is this week to narrow the role to read-only. Flagging it because you may hear it separately; please do not let it be conflated with this incident on the call.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**INC-2026-1109-01 — handoff / state of play**
**As at 14:20 UTC, 9 November 2026.** All times UTC, 2026-11-09.
**Status: OPEN — mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.**

### One-line state

All Batch API traffic is on the healthy fleet (cutover 12:58). Error rate on `POST /v1/batch/jobs` is 0.3% (baseline 0.2%) as of 14:12. Verification window closes **14:30**. Degraded fleet drained and out of rotation. Root cause untested.

### Impact (computed from `customer-impact.csv`, window 11:42–12:58)

- Batch API requests: **58,900**; failures: **17,602** → **29.9%** of Batch API requests failed.
- Batch API = 58,900 of 842,000 platform-wide requests in the window (**~7.0%**).
- **7 of 9** Batch API accounts failed, all on the degraded fleet. Two Batch API accounts: 0 failures.
- Per account: stark-industries 5,180/14,200 (11:43–12:57); contoso 3,410/9,400 (11:43–12:56); wayne-enterprises 2,790/7,850 (11:44–12:57); globex 2,240/6,100 (11:42–12:55); wonka-industries 2,020/5,900 (11:46–12:57); umbrella-health 1,560/4,300 (11:45–12:54); initech 402/1,150 (11:51–12:48).
- Platform-wide figure (842,000) is reference only. **Fleet membership is internal and is not a reporting basis** — use the aggregate Batch API figure above.

### Sequence

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 11:31 | `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` rollout completes — both fleets; 3 dependency bumps + DB pool max 80 → 24 per worker |
| 11:38 | Submission volume on fleet-a climbs to ~3x morning average (wonka scheduled job) |
| 11:42 | **Incident start.** `batch_api_5xx_rate` pages on fleet-a; 502s on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`. Priya acks |
| 11:44 | Confined to fleet-a; fleet-b clean — gateway and client SDK ruled out |
| 11:47 | Upstream storage ruled out (H3 rejected) |
| 11:55 | Status page update 1 published (Investigating) |
| 12:03 | Marcus: fleet-a workers queueing on DB connections; `r3` correlation noted, not tested |
| 12:05 | Status page update 2 published — **over-claimed cause identified and restoration within the hour** |
| 12:09 | Marcus freezes further cause statements; Ruth agrees to publish only from Tomas' approved list |
| 12:31 | Decision: **no rollback** of `r3` — preserve evidence; mitigate by moving traffic |
| 12:58 | **Mitigation:** all batch traffic → fleet-b; fleet-a drained. Error rate 0.4% within 2 min (baseline 0.2%) |
| 13:00 | **Verification window opens, closes 14:30** (90 min clean required by policy) |
| 13:20 | 0.3–0.4%; queue depth normal; no new customer reports |
| 13:52 | Re-drive ~60% complete; no failures on re-drive |
| 14:12 | 0.3%; 18 min left on window |
| 14:20 | **Now. Status update published (see below)** |

### Hypotheses — all untested

- **H1 (leading): `r3` connection-pool change.** For: 80 → 24 per worker, shipped 11:31, first page 11:42; workers observably queueing on DB connections. Against: same release on fleet-b, fleet-b healthy. **Rollback test has not been run.**
- **H2 (secondary): concentrated load on fleet-a.** For: ~3x morning average from 11:38. Against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.
- **H3 (rejected): upstream object storage.** Provider green; Files API on same provider healthy. Rejected 11:47.
- H1 and H2 may interact (lower ceiling biting under higher concurrency) — that is a third proposition, also untested.

### Open items at 14:20

1. **Verification window closes 14:30.** Nothing may be described as resolved before it closes clean. Check error rate at 14:30; if clean, decision on resolution status follows.
2. **Root cause.** Test H1 (rollback test on the drained fleet is now possible without customer impact) — still to be run. H2/H1 interaction untested.
3. **fleet-a return to rotation.** Blocked on root cause being understood; fleet-a is drained and holding no traffic.
4. **Re-drive of failed jobs.** ~60% at 13:52, no failures on re-drive. Confirm completion.
5. **Status page.** I published an update at 14:20 from the cleared list only, superseding the 12:05 post. Next update due **by 15:00 UTC** — Ruth to publish, and only from Tomas' approved list (per the 12:10 agreement).
6. **Contoso.** I am replying to TKT-8903 and TKT-8907 directly. **Do not** answer the SLA/credit question elsewhere; Schedule B.5 determination is a month-end process, and no determination is to be offered today.
7. **Umbrella-health (TKT-8904)** — compliance export due today; **wonka-industries (TKT-8912)** asking whether to resubmit failed submissions; **globex (TKT-8918)** asking if they were affected (globex data is in the impact file). All three are in the support queue with Tomas; note none of these are on my approved-to-send list, so route any reply through Tomas.
8. **SEC-411** — batch worker DB role has read+write on the billing schema, no business reason, unrelated to this incident. Marcus owns, target this week. Keep separate from INC-2026-1109-01.

### Comms rules in force (unchanged)

The cleared list is the **whole** of what may be said externally: (1) incident affecting the Batch API + start time; (2) mitigation applied and service recovering; (3) monitoring before confirming recovery; (4) further update with a stated time; (5) to a named customer, that account's own impact figures. **No cause statements until Marcus confirms.** No fleet names externally. The aggregate 29.9% figure and Marcus's ~16:00 internal estimate are internal only.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**To:** Contoso Ltd — Batch API incident correspondence
**Re:** Batch API incident — your account impact and current status (ref INC-2026-1109-01; your tickets TKT-8903, TKT-8907)

Dear Contoso team,

Thank you for contacting us today. This response covers both of your tickets — TKT-8903, opened at 11:58 UTC, and TKT-8907, opened at 12:26 UTC.

**What has happened**

There is an incident affecting the Batch API. It started at **11:42 UTC today, 9 November 2026**.

**Your account's impact**

During the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC today), your account made 9,400 Batch API requests, of which **3,410 returned errors (36.3%)**. Your first failed request was at 11:43 UTC and your last at 12:56 UTC.

**Current status**

A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before confirming recovery. We will send you a further update by **15:00 UTC today**.

**Your question about service credits (TKT-8907)**

Under Schedule B of your Master Services Agreement, Monthly Availability for a calendar month is determined by Northstar from its own service records **after the end of that calendar month**, and the figure is published within 10 business days of month end. We are therefore not able to confirm today whether the 99.9% commitment has been met for November, or what credit, if any, applies — no determination has been made.

Once the November figure is published, you will have 30 days from that publication to submit any credit claim, as set out in Schedule B.5. We will ensure the published figure and its basis are provided to you in accordance with your agreement.

We will come back to you with a further update by 15:00 UTC today, and will follow up when the November availability figure is published.

Kind regards,

Northstar Support
Reference: INC-2026-1109-01 | Tickets TKT-8903, TKT-8907
